title: AWS provider onboarding completes end-to-end from credential entry through a successful connection test
description: Covers the full path: submit credentials on /cloud-posture/configure, the backend stages them to Vault, calls Prowler's credential-validate endpoint (real AWS STS GetCallerIdentity, not simulated), and persists connectionHealth back onto the config.
preconditions: A project exists with no cloud provider configured yet
steps: Navigate to /cloud-posture/configure and select AWS
Enter accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, region='us-east-1', accountId='123456789012'
Click 'Test Connection'
On success, click 'Save Configuration'
expectedResult: Test connection returns success within the 15s timeout window; providers.aws.credentialConfigured becomes true; connectionHealth.status='verified' and lastTestedAt is set; the raw credential bundle is never present in any API response (only has*/isConfigured booleans).

title: Failed connection test surfaces a friendly error and leaves no orphaned Vault secret
description: config.controller.js stages raw credentials to a per-operation Vault path before calling Prowler's /internal/credentials/validate, then destroys the staged secret in a finally block regardless of outcome. Verifies the user-facing failure path and the secret-cleanup guarantee together.
preconditions: vibrantix-prowler service is unreachable or returns a validation failure for the submitted credentials
steps: On /cloud-posture/configure, submit AWS credentials with a deliberately invalid secretAccessKey
Click 'Test Connection'
Inspect the response and, if possible, the Vault path used for staging
expectedResult: UI shows 'Credential validation service unavailable. Please try again later.' (or the specific AWS rejection reason) without the app hanging past ~15s; providers.aws.credentialConfigured is not set to true; the staged Vault secret no longer exists after the call returns.

title: Manually triggered scan progresses queued to running to completed and findings become visible on the dashboard
preconditions: A project has a configured and verified AWS provider
steps: From the Cloud Posture dashboard, click 'Run Scan' for the AWS provider
Poll the scan detail page at /cloud-posture/scans/[scanId] until status leaves the active set
Once status is 'completed', return to the main dashboard
expectedResult: Scan record transitions through the active-status set (queued/running/processing/processing_results) and lands on 'completed'; the dashboard's overallComplianceScore, criticalFindings count, and service breakdown all update to reflect the new Finding documents without a manual page reload being required to see fresh data on next navigation.

title: Cancelling a running scan moves it to 'cancelling' and Prowler acknowledgement finalizes it to 'cancelled'
description: controlScan (scan.controller.js) only accepts cancel from the active-transition set and flips status to 'cancelling' first; a 404 from Prowler's cancel call is only treated as final confirmation when the scan has none of execution.attemptId/environment/queueJobId/leaseExpiresAt set (legacy-scan safety check) — otherwise it stays 'cancelling' for the reconciler.
preconditions: A scan is currently in status 'running' for a project the tester administers
steps: Open /cloud-posture/scans/[scanId] for the running scan
Click 'Cancel Scan'
Observe the status immediately after the click, then again after a few seconds
expectedResult: Status flips to 'cancelling' immediately; within a short interval it resolves to 'cancelled' once Prowler confirms the underlying job stopped. A second cancel attempt while already 'cancelling' does not throw a 409 conflict (idempotent no-op), but cancelling an already-terminal scan (e.g. 'completed') is rejected.

title: A completed scan's findings propagate to ISO 27001 control coverage on the compliance map within the same session
description: On scan completion, _fireCloudPostureComplianceSync (scan.controller.js) resolves each finding's checkId via findingCheckId(), joins to scanner_check_master.uclMappings, validates against ucl_master_v2, and calls client-compliance-sync.service's onCloudPostureScanCompleted to update ClientControl.scores.cloud. Sync is guarded by scan.metadata.complianceSyncFired so it only runs once per scan.
preconditions: ISO 27001 framework is activated for the project
A control mapped via scanner_check_master.uclMappings currently shows no cloud-sourced coverage
steps: Trigger and wait for a scan to reach 'completed' for the provider covering that control's check
Without reloading the browser session, navigate to /grc-framework/[id]/compliance-map
Locate the mapped control
expectedResult: The control's cloud coverage score reflects the scan's dominant pass/fail outcome for that check (FAIL if failCount>passCount, else PASS if passCount>0, else SKIP). Re-running the same completed scan's sync logic a second time does not double-count or duplicate the update (idempotency via complianceSyncFired).

title: Navigating dashboard to provider view to service to a security check surfaces the finding's CIS/ISO reference and remediation text
preconditions: A completed scan exists with at least one FAIL finding on a known service (e.g. S3)
steps: From the Cloud Posture dashboard, click into the AWS provider card
Filter or locate the S3 service row and open it
Open the failing security check's detail view
expectedResult: The check detail shows status FAIL, the resource(s) affected, the CIS/ISO27001/SOC2 framework tags carried in prowlerRaw (CheckCIS/CheckISO27001/CheckSOC2), and Prowler's static remediation/recommendation text (finding.recommendation) — not a blank or AI-generated field.

title: A recurring scan schedule actually fires at its next run time and updates lastRunStatus
description: scan-scheduler.job.js (started at vibrantix-backend/src/index.js:369) polls CloudPostureScan docs with status='scheduled_recurring' and schedule.nextRun <= now every 5s under a Redis distributed lock, claims via findOneAndUpdate, and calls prowlerService.triggerScan. Regression guard: an earlier internal audit incorrectly claimed schedules never execute — this case protects the fix.
preconditions: A project has a recurring scan schedule configured with frequency='hourly' and nextRun set to a few seconds in the past
steps: Wait for the scheduler's 5-second poll interval to pass
Query the scan record for that project/schedule
expectedResult: A new scan is created and triggered via prowlerService.triggerScan; the schedule document's metadata.lastRun is updated to the current time, metadata.runCount increments by 1, and metadata.lastRunStatus reflects the trigger outcome. nextRun advances per nextRun()'s hourly cadence (+1 hour).

title: Dashboard blends AWS and GCP compliance scores as an unweighted average across providers
description: getDashboardStats computes overallComplianceScore as avg(providers[].complianceScore) with no resource-count weighting. Documents current behavior end-to-end so a small GCP footprint doesn't silently get masked or over-weighted without anyone noticing the formula.
preconditions: One org has both AWS (large footprint, e.g. 1000+ resources, complianceScore=90%) and GCP (small footprint, e.g. 5 resources, complianceScore=40%) configured and scanned
steps: Open the Cloud Posture dashboard for that org
Read the overall security score
Compare it against a manually computed resource-weighted average
expectedResult: Overall score equals the simple average of the two providers' complianceScore values (e.g. (90+40)/2=65), not a resource-weighted figure closer to AWS's 90. This is documented current behavior, not a defect fix verification — flag to product if resource-weighting is later desired.
